# Azure Resource Manager Private DNS client library for Java

Azure Resource Manager Private DNS client library for Java

For documentation on how to use this package, please see [Azure Management Libraries for Java](https://aka.ms/azsdk/java/mgmt).

## Getting started

### Prerequisites

- [Java Development Kit (JDK)][jdk] with version 8 or above
- [Azure Subscription][azure_subscription]

### Adding the package to your product

[//]: # ({x-version-update-start;com.azure.resourcemanager:azure-resourcemanager-privatedns;current})
```xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>com.azure.resourcemanager</groupId>
    <artifactId>azure-resourcemanager-privatedns</artifactId>
    <version>2.54.0-beta.1</version>
</dependency>
```
[//]: # ({x-version-update-end})

### Include the recommended packages

Azure Management Libraries require a `TokenCredential` implementation for authentication and an `HttpClient` implementation for HTTP client.

[Azure Identity][azure_identity] package and [Azure Core Netty HTTP][azure_core_http_netty] package provide the default implementation.

### Authentication

Microsoft Entra ID token authentication relies on the [credential class][azure_identity_credentials] from [Azure Identity][azure_identity] package.

Azure subscription ID can be configured via `AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` environment variable.
Azure tenant ID can be configured via `AZURE_TENANT_ID` environment variable.

Assuming the use of the `DefaultAzureCredential` credential class, the client can be authenticated using the following code:

```java readme-sample-authenticate
AzureProfile profile = new AzureProfile(AzureCloud.AZURE_PUBLIC_CLOUD);
TokenCredential credential = new DefaultAzureCredentialBuilder()
    .authorityHost(profile.getEnvironment().getActiveDirectoryEndpoint())
    .build();
PrivateDnsZoneManager manager = PrivateDnsZoneManager
    .authenticate(credential, profile);
```

The sample code assumes global Azure. Please change `AzureEnvironment.AZURE` variable if otherwise.

See [Authentication][authenticate] for more options.

omissions.explanation: The record-set wrapper splits a supplied TXT value into 250-character chunks and stores those chunks in a TxtRecord before a record-set operation.
omissions.handwrittenRationale: The implementation method has no @Generated annotation, but this standalone wrapper has no neighboring annotated members or customization script establishing that the chunking was handwritten rather than emitted by the management-plane generator.

omissions.explanation: Updating a record set first fetches the existing resource, merges staged fields and record additions, removes matching A, AAAA or MX records, and then submits a create-or-update request.
omissions.handwrittenRationale: The wrapper methods explicitly combine a read with client-side merge and removal logic, but the captured implementation files lack direct evidence distinguishing handwritten fluent wrappers from generator-emitted management SDK implementations.

omissions.explanation: The zone wrapper snapshots tags on entering update mode and skips the service update call when an existing zone's tags remain unchanged.
omissions.handwrittenRationale: The conditional no-op and tag snapshot are explicit in the implementation, but the captured source and generation context do not establish whether these wrapper methods are handwritten rather than generator-produced.

omissions.explanation: The zone's paged record-set listing maps each returned inner record to a concrete public record-set wrapper based on its DNS record type.
omissions.handwrittenRationale: The page-item switch and concrete wrapper construction are present in the implementation, but their provenance is uncertain without a customization script, annotated-neighbor signal, or generator output comparison.

limitations: Coverage is partial: 111 discovered files, 79 eligible files, twelve source captures, 32 explicit skipped files and zero extraction errors. No capture is flagged as an excerpt. Neither these captures nor an empty findings array establish absence of customizations in this library.

All twelve captured entries have kind unknown and contain unannotated fluent facade implementations. No captured customization script, generated baseline, or contrast between generated and unannotated members establishes handwritten provenance. Observable algorithms, specialized defaults and absence of @Generated throughout a file are not alone proof of handwritten customization; uncertain claims are omitted as required by the supplied prompt.

The AAAA and A record-set implementations project address strings into new unmodifiable lists, append pending records to retrieved records and remove case-insensitive matches before clearing pending changes. MX exposes an unmodifiable list view and matches removals using exchange plus nonnull matching preference; CNAME replaces the pending canonical name and resets its staging model. These distinct visible behaviors are not attributed to handwritten edits without provenance. Unmodifiable list views are not described as deep immutable snapshots.

PrivateDnsRecordSetImpl stages record additions/removals and metadata changes, reads the current resource before update, applies metadata removals/additions and a pending TTL, then delegates to type-specific prepareForUpdate. It forwards ETagState-derived arguments and clears ETag state on successful mapped create/update responses. The ETagState implementation and inherited task/lifecycle details are absent; exact conditional-header policy and failure-time cleanup are not inferred.

The base record-set helper splits nonnull TXT input using a 250-position regular expression, whereas withoutText(String) stages a single supplied string and delegates to the list overload. This does not establish a byte-length guarantee or complete TXT removal matching semantics: TxtRecordSetImpl was explicitly skipped. Primitive TTL defaults, aliases, child keys and ordinary reactive delegation likewise lack handwritten attribution.

PrivateDnsRecordSetsImpl sets a 3600-second default TTL for inline definitions and delegates definitions, updates and removals to inherited helpers. PrivateDnsZoneImpl snapshots tags before update, skips the zone update call when tags compare equal, forwards ETag arguments, clears child collections after post-run, rebuilds typed record collections after refresh and maps listed records to type-specific wrappers. These concrete convenience, optimization and result-shaping behaviors are visible but their handwritten ownership and uncaptured inherited behavior are unresolved. PagedFlux/PagedIterable use alone is not a custom paginator.

All three complete generation contexts and all 32 skipped path/reason entries were read. The POM configures dependencies, tests and coverage exclusions; the README shows authentication; tsp-location identifies a specification revision. None proves a captured per-method edit. The uncaptured record subclasses, virtual-network-link implementations, public interfaces, manager and shared dependency implementations prevent exhaustive discovery or broader lifecycle claims. No external URL, source, history or generator baseline was fetched, and no package-wide LRO, paging or authentication absence claim is made.

No original analyst proposals were supplied, so there are no decisions or accepted/revised findings; all four omission candidates are inconclusive and uncounted pending independent confirmation of handwritten ownership.
Coverage is partial: 12 of 79 eligible source files were captured out of 111 discovered, and 32 named files were skipped for review budget. No package-wide absence or completeness claim is possible.

The captured implementation wrappers and pom.xml, README.md, and tsp-location.yaml provide no decisive provenance for the candidate methods; absence of @Generated alone does not distinguish handwritten changes from management-plane generated fluent implementations.
